To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we found a clear successional signature for the abundance and distribution patterns of genes that are involved in the microbially mediated nitrogen cycle in a salt marsh chronosequence, and that this signature is strongly related to shifts in soil physico- chemical properties.

we reconstructed the genetic potential of microorganisms that mediate nitrogen cycling in a pristine salt marsh chronosequence and that this potential is strongly linked to successional changes in soil properties.

the structure of the N cycling microbial community is strongly related to soil nitrogen, salinity, and pH, which is reflected in the distribution of N cycle genes across a salt marsh successional chronosequence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ecological and evolutionary processes that shape the structure and function of microbial communities involved in N cycling in coastal ecosystems.
the genetic potential of microorganisms that are potentially responsible for the N cycling processes in salt marshes.
the genetic potential of the microbially mediated nitrogen cycle in a pristine salt marsh ecosystem.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the genetic potential for N cycling is not only dependent on soil physicochemical properties, but also on historical contingency and ecosystem development, which are both important factors that should be considered when developing management plans for salt marshes.
this study provides a unique and comprehensive view on how the genetic potential of microorganisms involved in nitrogen cycling is distributed and structured in a salt marsh ecosystem.
the genetic potential for nitrogen cycling in salt marshes is strongly related to soil physico-chemistry, but also to the successional stage of the ecosystem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the genetic potential for N cycling processes in a pristine salt marsh is strongly related to soil nitrogen levels (e.g., NO3− and NH4+), soil pH and salinity.
the distribution and abundance patterns of N cycling genes are highly dependent on soil physico-chemistry, which in turn are strongly related to ecosystem age.

salt marshes are a highly diverse environment, where the distribution and abundance (i.e., the genetic potential) of microorganisms involved in N cycling is highly dynamic and is shaped by the soil physico- chemical characteristics, as well as by the successional trajectory of the ecosystem.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the assembly and dynamics of N cycling genes in coastal ecosystems are strongly linked to environmental conditions, and that the successional trajectories are not necessarily driven by the presence of a single microbial species or group of species.
the genetic potential of N cycling microorganisms is highly dynamic and that the distribution and abundance are strongly influenced by soil physico-chemistry and ecosystem age.
the ecological assembly of microbial communities involved in the N cycle is not only determined by soil physico-chemistry, but is also shaped by the historical contingency of the ecosystem.
